To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new method to characterize recombination centres in solar cells, and that we have identified and characterized the dominant recombination centres in Si, GaP and InGaP solar cells.
the irradiation-induced defects in Si, GaP and InGaP are characterized by a single recombination centre with a concentration of the order of 10 ^{14} cm ^{−3}.

the recombination centres created by electron irradiation have electron capture cross sections of 10−13 cm2 and hole capture cross section of 10−15 cm2 and that they have an energy level located 0.4 eV from the valence band in Si and GaP, 0.3 eV in GaAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of defects introduced by irradiations in semiconductors, with particular emphasis on the characterization of recombination defects.

two main topics: 1) the characterization of recombination centers induced by irradiation in solar cells; 2) the optimization of the fabrication process of solar cells in order to improve the radiation resistance.
the development of new materials and devices, based on the use of III-V compounds and silicon, for the conversion of solar energy into electricity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can identify the dominant recombination centre in Si as a divacancy and the dominant recombination centres in InGaP and GaAs as a gallium interstitial and an arsenic vacancy, respectively.
the method is very powerful, and the recombination centres can be characterized with a high accuracy.
the recombination centres are not only the vacancy, but also the vacancy-oxygen and vacancy-carbon complexes.

the recombination centres are not only the vacancy-related defects (V and V-O complexes) but also other defects, which have not yet been characterized.
